Converts 2-succinylbenzoate (OSB) to 2-succinylbenzoyl-CoA (OSB-CoA) (PubMed:22109989, PubMed:26394156, PubMed:30912442, PubMed:8626063). The reaction proceeds in two steps; in the first adenylation step, OSB reacts with Mg(2+)-ATP to form the tightly bound adenylate intermediate, OSB-AMP, which after the release of diphosphate reacts with coA in the second thioesterification step to form OSB-CoA and AMP (Probable)

Inhibited by OSB-AMS (o-succinylbenzoate-adenosine monophosphate sulfamate) and its negatively charged keto acid derivatives, but the neutral derivatives showed lower inhibitory potential (PubMed:22109989, PubMed:26394156, PubMed:30912442). These inhibitors also exhibit potential antibacterial activity against E.coli, B.subtilis, M.tuberculosis, and S.aureus (PubMed:22109989, PubMed:26394156)
kcat is 46 min(-1) with OSB as substrate.
